style: Say brightly and clearly, like an upbeat tour guide
lines: Welcome to Anchorage, Alaska. Pick something to drop, then tap Drop.
Straight down.
Straight down again, just like in Alaska.
Down under, it still falls straight down to the ground.
Even in Antarctica, straight down along the plumb line.
Now tap Mark on globe.
Drag the arrow the way the apple fell there, then tap Record.
Recorded.
Not quite. Here is the yard turned to sit on the globe. Line the arrow up with its plumb line.
Pick the next school, then tap Drop.
All four schools are recorded. Tap Zoom out.
Watch what happens when we make the arrows longer.
They all meet at one spot, the center of Earth.
So down is not one direction in space. Down is toward Earth's center, wherever you stand.
This is all of Earth. Drag to spin it, or tap the globe to stand a kid anywhere.
Build your argument. Tap a claim, then tap at least three place cards.
Tap Check claim to test it against your arrows.
Your claim fits every arrow. Now tap Test it.
The dashed arrows miss your evidence. Try a claim that fits all of it.
A new place. Drag the arrow to show which way down is there, then tap Predict.
Hit. Your claim predicted it.
Missed. See where the plumb line really points.
Three in a row. Your claim keeps predicting new places. That's a strong argument.
Finish your reasoning in the box to complete the card.
Tap Next place.
Record at least three places in Drop first. Tap Go to Drop.
Same apple, three worlds. Tap Drop all.
The Moon's apple is slowest, but on every world it falls toward the center.
